summary: The candidate correctly fixes split end-marker leakage and passes its focused and legacy tests, but independent original-contract cases still fail. It is a partial fix, not a full resolution.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced split end-marker corruption on the recorded base; also measured all-marker one-character fragmentation, nested long JSON, singular section markers, and a 600,000-character unclosed section.
The required split-end assertion passed. Independent observations still failed one-character marker fragmentation, singular-marker cleanliness, and bounded unclosed-section handling.
Candidate regression suite: 63 tests and 7 subtests passed.
Confirmed import from candidate repository source: /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/function_call/kimik2_detector.py.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and candidate change are pure Python parser behavior; no GPU execution was relevant or claimed. Environment inspection found one AMD Instinct MI350X (assigned gfx950).

remaining_counterexamples: One-character-at-a-time fragmentation of the complete wire format yields zero calls and leaks markers into normal_text.
An unclosed section containing 600,000 argument characters remains buffered in full (600,072 bytes) and emits no normal text; no configurable safety valve exists.
Singular K2-Thinking section markers tool_call_section_begin/tool_call_section_end remain in normal_text instead of being recognized or stripped.
Explicit cross-request detector reset/isolation is not added by the candidate; current_tool_id remains advanced after a completed section.
remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K2/K2.5 weights were available, so model semantic accuracy and real token emission were not tested.
No HTTP client/serving-path or multi-turn agent UI reproduction was performed; deterministic parser increments were tested directly.
The available single gfx950 AMD GPU differs from the reported 8x H100/H200/B200 environments; distributed behavior is unverified.
No native code changed, and therefore no native rebuild was applicable.
